records.name: Kansas
records.summary: Kansas's SB 244 (signed February 2026) is among the harshest instruments a traveller can meet: it confines trans people to birth-sex facilities in government buildings and voids state-issued IDs with corrected markers — licences invalid from 26 February 2026, no grace period, holders notified. The law also creates a private right of action under which anyone may sue a person they suspect of a violation for about $1,000 — a bounty-style exposure that the February 2026 legal-risk assessment singled out as the cycle's first 'Do Not Travel' addition, warning it 'could meaningfully affect interstate travel'.

sources.summary: ACLU of Kansas SB 244 FAQ: the law confines trans people to birth-sex facilities with new civil and criminal penalties; bars updating driver's licences or state IDs and invalidates existing licences whose gender marker is inconsistent with sex at birth — the Department of Revenue has been mailing written notice and many holders have already been told their licence is now invalid.

Erin in the Morning legal-risk assessment (20 Feb 2026): Kansas escalated Worst Laws -> Do Not Travel — the first 'Do Not Travel' state added in a year — driven by the new bathroom-bounty law letting private individuals sue trans people encountered in wrong-sex facilities; directly the assessment this record quotes on interstate-travel exposure.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (HTTP 403); the underlying state-politics-news report covers two trans men who filed Doe v. State of Kansas within days of SB 244's enactment (late Feb 2026, ACLU and Ballard Spahr, Douglas County District Court), citing fear of violence under the bathroom-restriction and ID-invalidation law.

records.name: South Carolina
records.summary:
South Carolina's facility ban, enacted 2024, was expanded in 2026 to colleges and universities when the governor signed House Bill 4756 on May 15, 2026, requiring students in public schools, colleges and universities to use restrooms matching sex assigned at birth.

The July 2026 assessment counts the expansion, raising the state's tier to 'Worst Laws Passed'; South Carolina is part of the 18-state birth-sex-definition group and scores below the national score 0.36.

sources.summary: July 2026 anti-trans national risk assessment: South Carolina is called out for expanding its bathroom ban to universities (campus settings added to the pre-existing restriction); the assessment's rubric ranks states on adult and youth law severity by reading bills, and South Carolina's expansion places it among the escalating states rather than the harshest tier.

ACLU of South Carolina (May 18, 2026): Governor Henry McMaster signed House Bill 4756 into law on Friday May 15, 2026, requiring transgender students in South Carolina public schools, colleges and universities to use restrooms matching their sex assigned at birth; ACLU frames it as discrimination against trans students in K-12 and higher education and notes the Senate amended the bill before passage. Press release dated May 18, 2026.
